claims.text: The dynamic behavior of solidified FeNiCrMn is governed by thermally activated dislocation glide.
Thermally activated dislocation glide controls the strength of solidified FeNiCrMn across temperature and strain-rate regimes.
Thermally activated dislocation glide controls the ductility of solidified FeNiCrMn across temperature and strain-rate regimes.
Dislocation density and arrangement mediate the response to changes in temperature and strain rate.
Changing temperature and strain rate will change the yield strength of solidified FeNiCrMn.
Changing temperature and strain rate will change the ultimate tensile strength of solidified FeNiCrMn.
Changing temperature and strain rate will change the ductility of solidified FeNiCrMn.
The proposed hypothesis is applicable from -200°C to 500°C.
The proposed hypothesis is applicable over strain rates from 10^-4 s^-1 to 10^3 s^-1.
The proposed study uses room-temperature, quasi-static mechanical properties as its baseline.
Grain size, texture, and impurities may influence the dynamic behavior.
The hypothesis can be tested using uniaxial tension tests at varied temperatures and strain rates with in-situ microscopy and strain-field measurements.
A lack of correlation between mechanical-property changes and thermally activated dislocation glide would falsify the hypothesis.
